186	  - **`apps/landing`** : CMS, présentation et textes légaux (`start.qoe.fi`)
187	  - **`apps/feed`** : Flux lecteurs, SSO centralisé (`qoe.fi`)
188	  - **`apps/dashboard`** : Studio créateur et éditeur d'articles (`dashboard.qoe.fi`)
189	  - **`apps/admin`** : Pilotage admin et modération (`admin.qoe.fi`)
190	  - **`apps/web`** : Rendu des blogs créateurs (`*.qoe.fi`)
191	
192	### 5. tsconfig pragmatique
193	- `strict: true` ✅
194	- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` ❌ (trop strict pour v1, à réactiver)
195	- `noImplicitOverride` ❌ (idem)
196	- `skipLibCheck: true` ✅
197	- `transpilePackages: ["@qoe/*"]` dans next.config.ts de chaque application
198	
199	---
200	
201	## 🧪 Commandes utiles
202	
203	```bash
204	# Build complet
205	pnpm build
206	
207	# Typecheck
208	pnpm typecheck
209	
210	# Une seule app
211	pnpm --filter @qoe/landing build
212	pnpm --filter @qoe/feed build
213	pnpm --filter @qoe/dashboard build
214	pnpm --filter @qoe/admin build
215	pnpm --filter @qoe/web build
216	pnpm --filter @qoe/api build
217	
218	# Dev (HMR)
219	pnpm dev
220	
221	# Prisma
222	pnpm prisma:migrate
223	pnpm prisma:generate
224	pnpm prisma:studio
225	
226	# Docker
227	pnpm docker:dev
228	pnpm docker:prod:build
229	pnpm docker:prod:up
230	pnpm docker:seed
231	pnpm docker:backup
232	pnpm docker:deploy
233	```
234	
235	---
236	
237	## 📂 Fichiers clés à connaître
238	
239	| Fichier | Rôle |
240	|---------|------|
241	| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | Déclare les 17 workspaces |
242	| `turbo.json` | Pipeline de build (cache, parallélisme) |
243	| `prisma.config.ts` | Pointe vers `packages/db/prisma/` |
244	| `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` | **Source de vérité** du modèle de données |
245	| `packages/ui/src/index.ts` | Exports centralisés des composants UI partagés |
246	| `apps/landing/next.config.ts` | Config Next pour la landing |
247	| `apps/feed/next.config.ts` | Config Next pour le feed et l'auth |
248	| `apps/dashboard/next.config.ts` | Config Next pour le dashboard |
249	| `apps/admin/next.config.ts` | Config Next pour le panel admin |
250	| `apps/web/next.config.ts` | Config Next pour les blogs |
251	| `docker-compose.yml` | 11 services + 2 réseaux |
252	| `docker/caddy/Caddyfile` | Reverse proxy + TLS auto |
253	| `scripts/deploy.sh` | Deploy complet sur VPS |
254	
255	---
256	
257	## 🛠️ Scripts PowerShell (utiles)
258	
259	| Script | Description |
260	|--------|-------------|
261	| `scripts/cleanup-fantoms.ps1` | Supprime les re-exports fantômes (legacy) |
262	| `scripts/dedupe-prisma.ps1` | Déduplique le schema Prisma |
263	| `scripts/dedupe-ui.ps1` | Déduplique les composants UI partagés |
264	| `scripts/fix-implicit-any.ps1` | Ajoute `: any` aux callbacks Prisma |
265	| `scripts/deploy.sh` | Deploy complet sur VPS (Bash) |
266	| `scripts/seed-docker.sh` | Seed la DB (Bash) |
267	| `scripts/backup-postgres.sh` | Backup Postgres (Bash) |
268	| `scripts/wait-for-db.sh` | Attend que Postgres soit healthy (Bash) |
269	
270	---
271	
272	## 🗺️ Roadmap future
273	
274	### 🟡 Stubs à remplacer
275	- `apps/console/src/app/(reader)/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx` (version minimaliste)
276	- `apps/console/src/components/ui/SubscribeForm.tsx` (si pas migré)
277	
278	### 🟡 Migration shadcn/ui → `packages/ui/`
279	- ~30 fichiers shadcn dans `apps/console/src/components/ui/` à migrer progressivement
280	- Le pattern est en place (cf. AXE 2)
281	
282	### 🔮 Workers BullMQ
283	- `apps/workers/` existe (placeholder)
284	- Jobs : emails, AI embeddings, billing webhooks
285	
286	### 🔮 CI/CD
287	- GitHub Actions : `pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build` sur chaque PR
288	- Docker Hub : build + push automatique des images
289	
290	### 🔮 Tests E2E
291	- Playwright sur les flux critiques : onboarding, publish article, login, payment
292	
293	### 🔮 Mobile
294	- React Native ou Expo pour app mobile (utilise le même backend API)
295	
296	---
297	
298	## 📖 Documentation
299	
300	| Fichier | Contenu |
301	|---------|---------|
302	| [README.md](./README.md) | Vitrine du projet (Quick start, stack, structure) |
303	| [GETTING_STARTED.md](./GETTING_STARTED.md) | Guide de démarrage rapide multi-plateforme (Mac/Win) |
304	| [ACTIVATION.md](./ACTIVATION.md) | Comment démarrer (4 commandes) |
305	| [DOCKER.md](./DOCKER.md) | Architecture Docker, 11 services, dev/prod |
306	| [DEPLOYMENT.md](./DEPLOYMENT.md) | Déploiement production (VPS, DNS, SSL, backups) |
307	| [HANDOFF.md](./HANDOFF.md) | **Ce fichier** — passation + historique |
308	| [MIGRATION.md](./MIGRATION.md) | Migration monolithe → monorepo (historique) |
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 🎓 Leçons apprises
313	
314	### Ce qui a bien marché
315	- **Strangler Fig pattern** : migration sans interruption, chaque étape réversible
316	- **Source unique Prisma** : pas de drift entre `prisma/` racine et `packages/db/`
317	- **Composants partagés dès le début** : éviter la duplication cross-apps
318	- **Docker multi-target** : 1 seul Dockerfile pour 7 cibles (landing, feed, dashboard, admin, web, api, workers)
319	- **Caddy** : TLS automatique, pas de config Let's Encrypt à maintenir
320	
321	### Ce qui a été challengeant
322	- **Windows + pnpm** : EPERM aléatoires, parfois il faut retry `pnpm install`
323	- **Prisma + pnpm workspaces** : solution `paths` dans tsconfig + `transpilePackages`
324	- **Next.js 16 `typedRoutes`** : très strict sur les href, on a dû ajouter `as any`
325	- **Windows Defender EACCES** : bloque `pnpm dev` sur port 3000/3010 en local
326	- **Flags TS stricts** : `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` cause trop d'erreurs en v1
327	
328	### Pour le prochain projet
329	- **Commencer directement par le monorepo** dès le début (pas de monolithe)
330	- **Centraliser Prisma dès le jour 1** dans `packages/db/prisma/`
331	- **Pousser les composants dans `packages/ui/`** dès qu'ils sont utilisés par 2 apps
332	- **Activer Caddy** (pas nginx) pour le TLS auto
333	- **Utiliser pnpm** (pas npm/yarn) pour les workspaces
334	- **Utiliser Turborepo** pour le cache de build
335	
336	---
337	
338	## 🎉 Conclusion
339	
340	Le projet est dans un état **propre, scalable, fonctionnel**. Le prochain dev qui arrive a tout ce qu'il faut dans [README.md](./README.md) pour être opérationnel en 5 minutes.
341	
342	Bonne chance pour la suite ! 🚀

#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées

packages:

  - "apps/*"

  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  - "!**/node_modules"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- You can optionally specify a line offset and limit (especially handy for long files), but it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, WEBP) and presents them visually.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 300000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

tools.name: WebSearch

Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

items.description: Hostname to include or exclude, without protocol, path, or wildcard

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

items.description: Hostname to include or exclude, without protocol, path, or wildcard

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool with explore agent instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using Glob, Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already explored the codebase and finalized the plan you want the user to review
- This tool DOES take the plan content as the required plan parameter in ZCode
- Pass the complete plan in the plan field; the user will review that content before approving implementation
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of the plan parameter when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion before finalizing your plan
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

plan.description: The implementation plan to present to the user for approval.

tool.description: The tool this prompt applies to

prompt.description: Semantic description of the action, e.g. "run tests", "install dependencies"

allowedPrompts.description: Prompt-based permissions needed to implement the plan. These describe categories of actions rather than specific commands.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations

167	## 🔧 Décisions architecturales clés
168	
169	### 1. Monorepo Turborepo
170	- **6 apps/services** indépendants → scale horizontal et isolation totale par contexte métier
171	- **10 packages** partagés → code DRY, type-safety bout-en-bout
172	- **Cache Turbo** → rebuild incrémental (42s la 1ère fois, < 1s en cache hit)
173	
174	### 2. Source unique Prisma : `packages/db/prisma/`
175	- Schema, migrations, seed sont **dans le package `@qoe/db`**
176	- `prisma.config.ts` (racine) pointe vers ce package
177	- Docker `migrate` service : `prisma migrate deploy --schema=/app/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`
178	- Plus de duplication `prisma/` racine / `packages/db/prisma/`
179	
180	### 3. Composants UI partagés : `packages/ui/`
181	- `SocialIcon`, `TenantHeader`, `SubscribeForm` → partagés entre `feed`, `dashboard`, `admin`, et `web`
182	- Exports subpath : `import { SocialIcon } from "@qoe/ui"`
183	
184	### 4. Décomposition de la plateforme (migration v2)
185	- Le gros dossier legacy `apps/console` et le site `start` de `apps/web` ont été scindés :
186	  - **`apps/landing`** : CMS, présentation et textes légaux (`start.qoe.fi`)
187	  - **`apps/feed`** : Flux lecteurs, SSO centralisé (`qoe.fi`)
188	  - **`apps/dashboard`** : Studio créateur et éditeur d'articles (`dashboard.qoe.fi`)
189	  - **`apps/admin`** : Pilotage admin et modération (`admin.qoe.fi`)
190	  - **`apps/web`** : Rendu des blogs créateurs (`*.qoe.fi`)

266	| `scripts/seed-docker.sh` | Seed la DB (Bash) |
267	| `scripts/backup-postgres.sh` | Backup Postgres (Bash) |
268	| `scripts/wait-for-db.sh` | Attend que Postgres soit healthy (Bash) |
269	
270	---
271	
272	## 🗺️ Roadmap future
273	
274	### 🟡 Stubs à remplacer
275	- `apps/console/src/app/(reader)/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx` (version minimaliste)
276	- `apps/console/src/components/ui/SubscribeForm.tsx` (si pas migré)
277	
278	### 🟡 Migration shadcn/ui → `packages/ui/`
279	- ~30 fichiers shadcn dans `apps/console/src/components/ui/` à migrer progressivement
280	- Le pattern est en place (cf. AXE 2)
281	
282	### 🔮 Workers BullMQ
283	- `apps/workers/` existe (placeholder)
284	- Jobs : emails, AI embeddings, billing webhooks
285	
286	### 🔮 CI/CD
287	- GitHub Actions : `pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build` sur chaque PR
288	- Docker Hub : build + push automatique des images
289	
290	### 🔮 Tests E2E
291	- Playwright sur les flux critiques : onboarding, publish article, login, payment
292	
293	### 🔮 Mobile
294	- React Native ou Expo pour app mobile (utilise le même backend API)
295	
296	---
297	
298	## 📖 Documentation
299	
300	| Fichier | Contenu |
301	|---------|---------|
302	| [README.md](./README.md) | Vitrine du projet (Quick start, stack, structure) |
303	| [GETTING_STARTED.md](./GETTING_STARTED.md) | Guide de démarrage rapide multi-plateforme (Mac/Win) |
304	| [ACTIVATION.md](./ACTIVATION.md) | Comment démarrer (4 commandes) |
305	| [DOCKER.md](./DOCKER.md) | Architecture Docker, 11 services, dev/prod |
306	| [DEPLOYMENT.md](./DEPLOYMENT.md) | Déploiement production (VPS, DNS, SSL, backups) |
307	| [HANDOFF.md](./HANDOFF.md) | **Ce fichier** — passation + historique |
308	| [MIGRATION.md](./MIGRATION.md) | Migration monolithe → monorepo (historique) |
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 🎓 Leçons apprises
313	
314	### Ce qui a bien marché
315	- **Strangler Fig pattern** : migration sans interruption, chaque étape réversible
316	- **Source unique Prisma** : pas de drift entre `prisma/` racine et `packages/db/`
317	- **Composants partagés dès le début** : éviter la duplication cross-apps
318	- **Docker multi-target** : 1 seul Dockerfile pour 7 cibles (landing, feed, dashboard, admin, web, api, workers)
319	- **Caddy** : TLS automatique, pas de config Let's Encrypt à maintenir
320	
321	### Ce qui a été challengeant
322	- **Windows + pnpm** : EPERM aléatoires, parfois il faut retry `pnpm install`
323	- **Prisma + pnpm workspaces** : solution `paths` dans tsconfig + `transpilePackages`
324	- **Next.js 16 `typedRoutes`** : très strict sur les href, on a dû ajouter `as any`
325	- **Windows Defender EACCES** : bloque `pnpm dev` sur port 3000/3010 en local
326	- **Flags TS stricts** : `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` cause trop d'erreurs en v1
327	
328	### Pour le prochain projet
329	- **Commencer directement par le monorepo** dès le début (pas de monolithe)
330	- **Centraliser Prisma dès le jour 1** dans `packages/db/prisma/`
331	- **Pousser les composants dans `packages/ui/`** dès qu'ils sont utilisés par 2 apps
332	- **Activer Caddy** (pas nginx) pour le TLS auto
333	- **Utiliser pnpm** (pas npm/yarn) pour les workspaces
334	- **Utiliser Turborepo** pour le cache de build
335	
336	---
337	
338	## 🎉 Conclusion
339	
340	Le projet est dans un état **propre, scalable, fonctionnel**. Le prochain dev qui arrive a tout ce qu'il faut dans [README.md](./README.md) pour être opérationnel en 5 minutes.
341	
342	Bonne chance pour la suite ! 🚀

# =====================================================================
# 📦 pnpm-workspace.yaml — Définit les workspaces du monorepo qoe.fi
# =====================================================================
# 📖 pnpm workspaces permet de gérer plusieurs packages/apps dans
#    un seul repo avec un seul `node_modules` partagé (économie disque).
#
# 🎯 Tous les dossiers listés ici sont traités comme des packages :
#    - Tu peux importer `@qoe/db` depuis n'importe quelle app
#    - Une modif dans un package rebuild automatiquement
#
# 📖 Structure :
#    apps/*    → Les applications déployables (Next.js, Hono, workers)
#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées
#    workers/*  → Les workers asynchrones (optionnel v1)
# =====================================================================

packages:
  # 🟢 Applications déployables
  - "apps/*"

  # 📚 Bibliothèques partagées
  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  # ❌ Exclusions explicites (ne PAS traiter comme workspace)
  - "!**/node_modules"
  - "!**/dist"
  - "!**/.next"
  - "!**/build"
  - "!**/.turbo"

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool with explore agent instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using Glob, Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already explored the codebase and finalized the plan you want the user to review
- This tool DOES take the plan content as the required plan parameter in ZCode
- Pass the complete plan in the plan field; the user will review that content before approving implementation
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of the plan parameter when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion before finalizing your plan
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

Read relevant or handoff context from another persisted ZCode session. Use when the user references #sess_* or asks to continue from a specific prior session.

Available agent types and the tools they have access to:
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches - when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. 167	## 🔧 Décisions architecturales clés
168	
169	### 1. Monorepo Turborepo
170	- **6 apps/services** indépendants → scale horizontal et isolation totale par contexte métier
171	- **10 packages** partagés → code DRY, type-safety bout-en-bout
172	- **Cache Turbo** → rebuild incrémental (42s la 1ère fois, < 1s en cache hit)
173	
174	### 2. Source unique Prisma : `packages/db/prisma/`
175	- Schema, migrations, seed sont **dans le package `@qoe/db`**
176	- `prisma.config.ts` (racine) pointe vers ce package
177	- Docker `migrate` service : `prisma migrate deploy --schema=/app/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`
178	- Plus de duplication `prisma/` racine / `packages/db/prisma/`
179	
180	### 3. Composants UI partagés : `packages/ui/`
181	- `SocialIcon`, `TenantHeader`, `SubscribeForm` → partagés entre `feed`, `dashboard`, `admin`, et `web`
182	- Exports subpath : `import { SocialIcon } from "@qoe/ui"`
183	
184	### 4. Décomposition de la plateforme (migration v2)
185	- Le gros dossier legacy `apps/console` et le site `start` de `apps/web` ont été scindés :
186	  - **`apps/landing`** : CMS, présentation et textes légaux (`start.qoe.fi`)
187	  - **`apps/feed`** : Flux lecteurs, SSO centralisé (`qoe.fi`)
188	  - **`apps/dashboard`** : Studio créateur et éditeur d'articles (`dashboard.qoe.fi`)
189	  - **`apps/admin`** : Pilotage admin et modération (`admin.qoe.fi`)
190	  - **`apps/web`** : Rendu des blogs créateurs (`*.qoe.fi`)
191	
192	### 5. tsconfig pragmatique
193	- `strict: true` ✅
194	- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` ❌ (trop strict pour v1, à réactiver)
195	- `noImplicitOverride` ❌ (idem)
196	- `skipLibCheck: true` ✅

312	## 🎓 Leçons apprises
313	
314	### Ce qui a bien marché
315	- **Strangler Fig pattern** : migration sans interruption, chaque étape réversible
316	- **Source unique Prisma** : pas de drift entre `prisma/` racine et `packages/db/`
317	- **Composants partagés dès le début** : éviter la duplication cross-apps
318	- **Docker multi-target** : 1 seul Dockerfile pour 7 cibles (landing, feed, dashboard, admin, web, api, workers)
319	- **Caddy** : TLS automatique, pas de config Let's Encrypt à maintenir
320	
321	### Ce qui a été challengeant
322	- **Windows + pnpm** : EPERM aléatoires, parfois il faut retry `pnpm install`
323	- **Prisma + pnpm workspaces** : solution `paths` dans tsconfig + `transpilePackages`
324	- **Next.js 16 `typedRoutes`** : très strict sur les href, on a dû ajouter `as any`
325	- **Windows Defender EACCES** : bloque `pnpm dev` sur port 3000/3010 en local
326	- **Flags TS stricts** : `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` cause trop d'erreurs en v1
327	
328	### Pour le prochain projet
329	- **Commencer directement par le monorepo** dès le début (pas de monolithe)
330	- **Centraliser Prisma dès le jour 1** dans `packages/db/prisma/`

# =====================================================================
# 📦 pnpm-workspace.yaml — Définit les workspaces du monorepo qoe.fi
# =====================================================================
# 📖 pnpm workspaces permet de gérer plusieurs packages/apps dans
#    un seul repo avec un seul `node_modules` partagé (économie disque).
#
# 🎯 Tous les dossiers listés ici sont traités comme des packages :
#    - Tu peux importer `@qoe/db` depuis n'importe quelle app
#    - Une modif dans un package rebuild automatiquement
#
# 📖 Structure :
#    apps/*    → Les applications déployables (Next.js, Hono, workers)
#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées
#    workers/*  → Les workers asynchrones (optionnel v1)
# =====================================================================

packages:
  # 🟢 Applications déployables
  - "apps/*"

  # 📚 Bibliothèques partagées
  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  # ❌ Exclusions explicites (ne PAS traiter comme workspace)
  - "!**/node_modules"
  - "!**/dist"
  - "!**/.next"
  - "!**/build"
  - "!**/.turbo"

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool with explore agent instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using Glob, Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already explored the codebase and finalized the plan you want the user to review
- This tool DOES take the plan content as the required plan parameter in ZCode
- Pass the complete plan in the plan field; the user will review that content before approving implementation
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of the plan parameter when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion before finalizing your plan
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

1	# Feuille de route — Refonte du Dashboard Créateur qoe.fi
2	
3	> **Objectif :** livrer un dashboard créateur complet, à l'esthétique épurée/minimaliste
4	> (inspiration [`articles-client.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/articles-client.tsx)),
5	> procurant un sentiment de liberté. **Direction design retenue : neutre zinc/noir,
6	> vermillon `#EE4B2B` relégué à accent discret optionnel.**
7	>
8	> Stack : Next.js 16 (App Router) + Supabase Auth + Prisma + Server Actions + shadcn/ui.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 📊 État des lieux (constat initial)
13	
14	| Zone | État | Remarque |
15	|------|------|----------|
16	| [`articles`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/articles-client.tsx) | ✅ **Référence** | Style Apple-esque zinc épuré, CRUD complet, tabs textuels |
17	| [`articles/[id]`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/[id]/edit-article-client.tsx) | ⚠️ À vérifier | Éditeur Tiptap + paywall divider |
18	| [`articles/new`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/new/new-article-client.tsx) | ⚠️ À vérifier | Création article |
19	| [`(creator)/page.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/page.tsx) | ❌ Placeholder | Page d'accueil dashboard |

27	
28	**Conflit design majeur à résoudre en priorité :** la page de référence utilise des
29	hardcoded `zinc-*` qui contournent les tokens sémantiques (`--primary`, `--foreground`).
30	Il faut unifier tout le dashboard sur un **système de tokens neutres**.

34	## 🗺️ Roadmap par phases
35	
36	```mermaid
37	flowchart LR
38	    P0[Phase 0 — Fondations design] --> P1[Phase 1 — Layout & shell]
39	    P1 --> P2[Phase 2 — Page d'accueil]
40	    P2 --> P3[Phase 3 — Articles]

44	    P6 --> P7[Phase 7 — Settings & branding]

47	```

49	---

51	### Phase 0 — Fondations design system (PRÉREQUIS, bloque tout)
52	
53	> Sans cette phase, chaque page reproduira l'incohérence actuelle. C'est le socle.
54	
55	- [ ] **0.1** Réécrire [`globals.css`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/globals.css) : thème `:root` neutre
56	      zinc/noir (remplacer le "White & Red" vermillon). Garder le vermillon uniquement dans une
57	      variable `--accent-brand` optionnelle (utilisable via classe utilitaire `.accent-brand`).
58	- [ ] **0.2** Définir les tokens sémantiques définitifs : `--background`, `--foreground`,
59	      `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--primary` (= zinc-950), `--accent-brand` (vermillon, opt-in).
60	- [ ] **0.3** Créer un guide de style / cheatsheet (`apps/dashboard/STYLE.md`) référençant les
61	      patterns de la page articles : titre `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight`, sous-titre poétique
62	      `text-zinc-400 text-xs`, tabs textuels avec underline `layoutId`, liste `space-y-1` avec
63	      `border-b border-zinc-100/60`, statut "quiet dot" `h-1.5 w-1.5 rounded-full`.
64	- [ ] **0.4** Refactorer [`articles-client.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/articles-client.tsx)

147	## 🎯 Ordre de priorité recommandé
148	
149	1. **Phase 0** (bloquant) → unifier les tokens avant d'écrire toute nouvelle UI.
150	2. **Phase 1** → shell & composants réutilisables (investissement rentabilisé sur toutes les pages).

152	4. **Phase 2** → page d'accueil (première impression utilisateur).

159	## ⚙️ Principes directeurs (à respecter à chaque phase)

163	- **Tokens sémantiques > hardcoded** : jamais de `text-zinc-900` dans le nouveau code, toujours

165	- **Densité faible, respiration haute** : `space-y-12`, `py-6`, `max-w-3xl` pour le contenu de
166	  lecture, `max-w-5xl` pour les listes.

# =====================================================================
# 📦 pnpm-workspace.yaml — Définit les workspaces du monorepo qoe.fi
# =====================================================================
# 📖 pnpm workspaces permet de gérer plusieurs packages/apps dans
#    un seul repo avec un seul `node_modules` partagé (économie disque).
#
# 🎯 Tous les dossiers listés ici sont traités comme des packages :
#    - Tu peux importer `@qoe/db` depuis n'importe quelle app
#    - Une modif dans un package rebuild automatiquement
#
# 📖 Structure :
#    apps/*    → Les applications déployables (Next.js, Hono, workers)
#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées
#    workers/*  → Les workers asynchrones (optionnel v1)
# =====================================================================

packages:
  # 🟢 Applications déployables
  - "apps/*"

  # 📚 Bibliothèques partagées
  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  # ❌ Exclusions explicites (ne PAS traiter comme workspace)
  - "!**/node_modules"
  - "!**/dist"
  - "!**/.next"
  - "!**/build"
  - "!**/.turbo"

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool with explore agent instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using Glob, Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already explored the codebase and finalized the plan you want the user to review
- This tool DOES take the plan content as the required plan parameter in ZCode
- Pass the complete plan in the plan field; the user will review that content before approving implementation
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of the plan parameter when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion before finalizing your plan
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

1	# Feuille de route — Refonte du Dashboard Créateur qoe.fi
2

4	> (inspiration [`articles-client.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/articles-client.tsx)),
5	> procurant un sentiment de liberté. **Direction design retenue : neutre zinc/noir,
6	> vermillon `#EE4B2B` relégué à accent discret optionnel.**
7	>
8	> Stack : Next.js 16 (App Router) + Supabase Auth + Prisma + Server Actions + shadcn/ui.
9	
10	---

# =====================================================================
# 📦 pnpm-workspace.yaml — Définit les workspaces du monorepo qoe.fi
# =====================================================================
# 📖 pnpm workspaces permet de gérer plusieurs packages/apps dans
#    un seul repo avec un seul `node_modules` partagé (économie disque).
#
# 🎯 Tous les dossiers listés ici sont traités comme des packages :
#    - Tu peux importer `@qoe/db` depuis n'importe quelle app
#    - Une modif dans un package rebuild automatiquement
#
# 📖 Structure :
#    apps/*    → Les applications déployables (Next.js, Hono, workers)
#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées
#    workers/*  → Les workers asynchrones (optionnel v1)
# =====================================================================

packages:
  # 🟢 Applications déployables
  - "apps/*"

  # 📚 Bibliothèques partagées
  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  # ❌ Exclusions explicites (ne PAS traiter comme workspace)
  - "!**/node_modules"
  - "!**/dist"
  - "!**/.next"
  - "!**/build"
  - "!**/.turbo"

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool with explore agent instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using Glob, Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

## How This Tool Works

148	
149	1. **Phase 0** (bloquant) → unifier les tokens avant d'écrire toute nouvelle UI.

160

171	  l'interactivité (cf. pattern [`page.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/page.tsx)
172	  + [`articles-client.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/articles-client.tsx)).
173	- **Sécurité** : toute action serveur via [`requireUser`](../packages/auth/src/current-user.ts)
174	  de [`@qoe/auth`](../packages/auth) (déjà en place dans [`actions.ts`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/actions.ts)).

1 # Architecture — Système de Thème Unifié Multi-Apps qoe.fi 2 3 > **Vision :** un système de design tokens en couches, source unique de vérité, 4 > permettant de changer de thème (light/dark/futurs) de façon **unifiée sur toutes 5 > les apps**, tout en supportant le **branding par créateur** (blogs tenants) sans 6 > recodage. 7 > 8 > **Principe senior :** les composants ne connaissent que les **tokens sémantiques** 9 > (`text-foreground`, `bg-primary`). # =====================================================================
# 📦 pnpm-workspace.yaml — Définit les workspaces du monorepo qoe.fi
# =====================================================================
# 📖 pnpm workspaces permet de gérer plusieurs packages/apps dans
#    un seul repo avec un seul `node_modules` partagé (économie disque).
#
# 🎯 Tous les dossiers listés ici sont traités comme des packages :
#    - Tu peux importer `@qoe/db` depuis n'importe quelle app
#    - Une modif dans un package rebuild automatiquement
#
# 📖 Structure :
#    apps/*    → Les applications déployables (Next.js, Hono, workers)
#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées
#    workers/*  → Les workers asynchrones (optionnel v1)
# =====================================================================

packages:
  # 🟢 Applications déployables
  - "apps/*"

  # 📚 Bibliothèques partagées
  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  # ❌ Exclusions explicites (ne PAS traiter comme workspace)
  - "!**/node_modules"
  - "!**/dist"
  - "!**/.next"
  - "!**/build"
  - "!**/.turbo"

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool with explore agent instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using Glob, Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already explored the codebase and finalized the plan you want the user to review
- This tool DOES take the plan content as the required plan parameter in ZCode
- Pass the complete plan in the plan field; the user will review that content before approving implementation
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of the plan parameter when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion before finalizing your plan
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

148	
149	1. **Phase 0** (bloquant) → unifier les tokens avant d'écrire toute nouvelle UI.

172	  + [`articles-client.tsx`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/articles-client.tsx)).
173	- **Sécurité** : toute action serveur via [`requireUser`](../packages/auth/src/current-user.ts)
174	  de [`@qoe/auth`](../packages/auth) (déjà en place dans [`actions.ts`](../apps/dashboard/src/app/(creator)/articles/actions.ts)).

1 # Architecture — Système de Thème Unifié Multi-Apps qoe.fi 2 3 > **Vision :** un système de design tokens en couches, source unique de vérité, 4 > permettant de changer de thème (light/dark/futurs) de façon **unifiée sur toutes 5 > les apps**, tout en supportant le **branding par créateur** (blogs tenants) sans 6 > recodage. 7 > 8 > **Principe senior :** les composants ne connaissent que les **tokens sémantiques** 9 > (`text-foreground`, `bg-primary`). Ils n'ont jamais connaissance du thème concret 10 > (zinc, vermillon, dark…) ni du tenant. # =====================================================================
# 📦 pnpm-workspace.yaml — Définit les workspaces du monorepo qoe.fi
# =====================================================================
# 📖 pnpm workspaces permet de gérer plusieurs packages/apps dans
#    un seul repo avec un seul `node_modules` partagé (économie disque).
#
# 🎯 Tous les dossiers listés ici sont traités comme des packages :
#    - Tu peux importer `@qoe/db` depuis n'importe quelle app
#    - Une modif dans un package rebuild automatiquement
#
# 📖 Structure :
#    apps/*    → Les applications déployables (Next.js, Hono, workers)
#    packages/* → Les bibliothèques partagées
#    workers/*  → Les workers asynchrones (optionnel v1)
# =====================================================================

packages:
  # 🟢 Applications déployables
  - "apps/*"

  # 📚 Bibliothèques partagées
  - "packages/*"

  # ⚙️ Workers asynchrones (BullMQ, jobs, etc.)
  - "workers/*"

  # ❌ Exclusions explicites (ne PAS traiter comme workspace)
  - "!**/node_modules"
  - "!**/dist"
  - "!**/.next"
  - "!**/build"
  - "!**/.turbo"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- You can optionally specify a line offset and limit (especially handy for long files), but it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, WEBP) and presents them visually.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Write

Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: Edit

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 300000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.
